evaluation.full_model_answer:
**Introduction**
Constitutional governance in India requires continuous calibration between democratic responsiveness and institutional autonomy.

**[INITIAL VALUE-ADDITION BOX / SMART-ART]**
[1. Constitutional Articles: Art 14, 19, 21 | 2. Landmark Rulings: Kesavananda, Puttaswamy, ADR | 3. Reports: 2nd ARC, Punchhi Commission, Law Commission]

**1. Core Structural Mandates & Constitutional Principles**
• **Judicial Prudence**: Preserves fundamental rights against arbitrary executive or legislative incursions.
• **Institutional Integrity**: Mandates robust checks and balances to prevent concentration of unreviewable power.

**[EXAM-HALL SCHEMATIC]**
+------------------------------------------------+
|           INSTITUTIONAL CHECKS & BALANCES      |
|  Executive <---> Legislature <---> Judiciary   |
+------------------------------------------------+

**2. Systemic Challenges & Ground Realities**
• **Procedural Delays**: Bureaucratic bottlenecks impede timely grievance redressal and statutory compliance.
• **Capacity Deficits**: Subordinate administrative bodies require infrastructure and technical upgrades.

**3. Actionable Way Forward & Policy Roadmap**
• **Statutory Timelines**: Mandate time-bound processing for all official referrals.
• **Digital Governance Integration**: Leverage AI platforms for transparent tracking.

**Conclusion**
Institutional revitalization anchored in constitutional morality is the cornerstone of sustainable governance and Viksit Bharat @2047.
